cards.explanation: The answer is Edom. The very first verse says, "This is the account of Esau (that is, Edom)." (Genesis 36:1) Two names, one man. Verse 8 says it again, and verse 43 ends by calling Esau "…the father of the Edomites…" That's a name with a whole nation hanging off it, friends.

The answer is Ishmael. Verse 3 says Basemath is the "…daughter of Ishmael and sister of Nebaioth." (Genesis 36:3) Ishmael was Abraham's son (Genesis 25:12). So Esau's wife comes from Abraham's family, too. Notice the text names her brother, Nebaioth, as well.

The answer is in the land of Canaan. Verse 5 says these were the sons of Esau, "…who were born to him in the land of Canaan." (Genesis 36:5) All five of them, Eliphaz, Reuel, Jeush, Jalam and Korah, were born there before the big move. The family tree starts in Canaan and grows from there, bakers.

The answer is False. Verse 6 says Esau took "…his livestock, all his other animals, and all the property he had acquired in Canaan…" (Genesis 36:6) He didn't leave the herd behind. Verse 7 adds that their possessions were too great for them to dwell together. So the livestock went right along with him.

The answer is True. Verse 6 says Esau moved "…to a land far away from his brother Jacob." (Genesis 36:6) Then verse 8 says he settled in the area of Mount Seir. The text tells us where he went and how big the move was, friends. It doesn't say anything more about how the brothers felt.

The reason is that they own too much for the land to support. Verse 7 says, "For their possessions were too great for them to dwell together; the land where they stayed could not support them because of their livestock." (Genesis 36:7) Too many animals, not enough land. I've had a kitchen like that. Too many cookies, not enough counter.

The answer is the area of Mount Seir. Verse 8 says, "So Esau (that is, Edom) settled in the area of Mount Seir." (Genesis 36:8) Later the passage lists the sons of Seir the Horite, "…who were living in the land…" (Genesis 36:20) So Seir is a name worth remembering, friends. Esau shows up with all his stuff, and I think he needed every bit of that room.
